correctness.rationale: Every bond configuration has strictly positive weight. Hilbert–Schmidt convexity and empty-graph identity eliminate all nontrivial peripheral eigenphases. Each singleton edge Laplacian has a nontrivial two-point phase exactly off πZ. Rank-one edge-projection commutation plus connected line graph forces a scalar action on the span of edge differences; their common kernel is the uniform vector. Contractivity prevents peripheral Jordan blocks, conserved sector traces determine the limiting operator, and the n=2 π-resonance explicitly falsifies any graph-uniform extension. A numerical checker tested five graphs and verified nonuniform initial coherence; computations are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: The original model produced numerically flat vertex marginals but left the quantum-state limit unresolved. This result gives a global all-connected-graph stationary-channel classification, proves exactly when quantum coherence survives despite uniform vertex probabilities, extends robustness to heterogeneous bond survival probabilities, and sharpens a necessary universal step-size exclusion. The structural commutant lemma and full-density convergence are mathematically motivated, beyond a single numerical toy case.
